full_judgment:
3. The plaint case, in short, is that the land described in the 1st schedule of the plaint along with other land belonged to late Gopika Ramani Roy. He granted permanent pattani settlement of the said land to Krishna Kumar Dey Purokaistha by pattani deed dated 20.12.1925. Krishana Kumar died leaving two sons, Dinesh Chandra Dey Purokaistha and Paresh Chandra dey Purokais that as his sole heirs. The said two sons granted Dar pattani settlement of the first schedule land to Narendra Krishna Dutta by registered patta and Kabuliat dated 3.1.1930. Narendra Krishna Dutta entered into possession of the land and constructed residential quarters thereon and he possessed the land with structure through a monthly tenant named Surendra Kumar Das, a pleader of Sylhet District Bar. Dinesh and Paresh mortgaged the first schedule land and other lands to defendant No. 1, the Sylhet Cooperative land Mortgage Bank Ltd. by Mortgage deed dated 27.10.1930. The Derpattani holder Narendra Krishna Dutta also mortgaged the first schedule land and the structures to Sylhet Industrial Bank Ltd. by a registered deed of mortgage dated 20.3.1939. The mortgagor failed to pay the mortgage money and the mortgagee, the Sylhet Industrial Bank Ltd. filed Title Suit No. 33 of 1940 in the Vid Court of Subordinate Judge, Sylhet and obtained a decree. The said decree was put into execution in Title Execution Case No. 41 of 1942 and in execution preceding the decree holder Bank auction purchased the first schedule land and structures on 13.11.1943. The auction sale was confirmed and the delivery of possession was taken by the auction purchaser. The Sylhet Industrial Bank Ltd. could not take actual possession in the land and Surendra Kumar Das continued to remain in possession of the land. Surendra Kumer Das purchased the first schedule properties including in the benami of his sons Subendu Krishna Das Chowdhury and Sudhendu Kishore Das Chowdhury by Kabala dated 17th Aswin, 1351. B.S. and Surendra Kumar Das possessed the premises in his own right. It is asserted that Surendra Kumar Das left Sylhet after partition of the Subcontinent in 1947 letting out the premises to Sailesh Chandra Roy and Suresh Chandra Roy and possessed the premises through the said tenants. Then Surendra Kumar died in India sometimes prior to 9.5.1951 leaving six sons as his heirs. Out of the six sons four sons, namely, Swapon Krishna Das Chowdhury, Subrata Krishna Das Chowdhury, Susanta Krishna Das Chowdhury and Salil Krishna Das Chowdhury contracted to sell the first schedule land and structures to Rais Ali at a price of Tk. 1500 and on receipt of Tk. 1200 the said four sons executed a bainapatra on 3.4.1958 in favour of Rais Ali and put him in possession of the properties. The said four sons failed to execute the sale deed although the purchaser Rais Ali paid the balance amount of Tk. 300. Rais Ali having been in possession of the contracted land and structures for more than statutory period acquired hostile title by way of adverse possession in the property. Rais Ali himself resided in the property and also possessed through tenants. Thereafter Rais Ali sold eastern half of the first schedule land along with the structures to the plaintiff No. 1 by two kabalas dated 13.9.77 and 19.9.77. Rais Ali also sold the western half of the said property to the plaintiff No. 2 by two kabala dated 14.9.77 and 20.9.77 respectively and put the plaintiffs in possession of the said properties with the Bharatia Nurul Haque Chowdhury. The tenant Nurul Huq Chowdhury on 20.9.77 vacated the first schedule and since then the plaintiffs have been possessing the first schedule land and residing in the building on the eastern side of the land. The plaintiffs have been possessing the first schedule land for more than statutory period in their own right and adversely to others. On 24.9.77 Mr. A Sadrul Amin Chowdhury, an Advocate Commissioner along with Process Server of the Court went to the suit land and asked the plaintiffs to vacate the properties on the plea that the defendant No. 1 obtained a decree for khas possession in respect of the suit land against one Akaddas Ali Laskar in T.S. No. 56 of 1959. As the plaintiffs have been in possession in their own right they refuied to vacate the suit land. Thereafter the plaintiffs made search, inquiries and came to learn that the defendant No. 1 purchased the suit land and other lands from the defendant No. 2 and then secured a decree against Akaddas Ali in Title Suit No. 56 of 1959. The plaintiffs also came to learn that Sylhet Cooperative Land Mortgage Bank Ltd. obtained a decree against Dinesh, Parash, Surendra Kumar Das and two of his sons, namely, Subendhu Krishna Das Chowdhury and Sudhendu Kishore Das Chowdhury in Title Suit No. 72 of 1947 of the 2nd Court of Subordiante Judge, Sylhet and that the Bank filed Title Execution Case No. 54 of 1954 and obtained delivery possession on 27.12.1954 symbolically. The plaintiffs also learned that defendant No. 1 filed Title Execution Case No. 33 of 1977 in the 1st Court of Munsif, Sadar, Sylhet for taking delivery of Khas possession of the suit land. It is the further case of them plaintiff that in Title Suit No. 72 of 1977 the defendant No. 2 stated that Surendra Kumar Das purchased the first schedule land and structure’s in the benami of his sons Subendhu Krishan Das Chowdhury and Sudhendu Kishore Das Chowdhury and thus admitted that Surendra Kumar Das was the real purchaser of the Is' schedule land and structures from the Sylhet Industrial Bank Ltd. During the pendency of Title Suit No. 72 of 1947 Surendra Kumar Das died, his heirs were not substituted and as such the decree is null and void, Defendant No. 2 derivence right, title and interest in the first schedule land and defendant No. 2 had no saleable interest and the defendant No. 1 has acquired no right, title and interest in the said land by her alleged purchase. The decree obtained in Title Suit No. 56 of 1959 in respect of second schedule of land is collusive and fraudulent and the plaintiffs are not bound by that decree. 

 4. The defendant No. 1 Rabeya Khanem Chowdhury contested the suit by filing written statement. In the preliminary objection in term alia, the defendant pleaded that the suit is barred by limitation. The defendants case is that 1st Schedule land belonged to Kumar Gupika Raman Roy and Redhika Mohan Dutta having 9 annas and 7 annas share respectively. Krishna Kumar Dey Purakaistha took. Permanent pattani settlement from the said owners by two deeds dated 21.12.1925 and 17.3.1926. The first schedule land along with other lands were mortgaged by Dinesh and Paresh Chandra Dey Purakaistha to the defendant No. 2, the Sylhet Cooperative Land Mortgage Bank Ltd. The mortgaged money having not been paid by the mortgagers the Bank obtained a mortgage decree and in execution of the decree Bank purchased the said land in Title Execution Case Nos. 180 of 1936 and 182 of 1936. The sale certificate was granted on 18.11.1936 and the possession was delivered on 16.3.1937 to the said Bank. Subendhu Krishna Das Chowdhury and Sudhendu Kishore Das Chowdhury purchased the schedule land from Sylhet Industrial Bank Ltd. with their own money and for their own benefit and their father Surendra Kumar Das had no interest in the land purchased by them. As Surendra Das has been in possession of the structures he was impleaded along with his two sons as defendant in title Suit No. 72 of 1947. The said Title suit was decreed on 12.5.1952 and decree was awarded for recovery of Khas possession. That Suredra died prior to 9.5.1951 is not correct. The decree obtained in Title Suit No.72 of 1947 was put into execution being Title execution Case No. 54 of 1954 and pursuant to that proceeding delivery of possession was given to the defendant No. 2 Bank and the defendant No. 2 Bank and the defendant No. 2 sold the suit land along with other land by registered kabala dated 7.11.1955 to the defendant No. 1. Thereafter the defendant No. 1. Instituted Title Suit No. 56 of 1959 in the Court of Munsif, Sadar, Sylhet against Akaddas Ali and Abdul Musabbir in which Subendu and Sudhendu were impleaded as defendants. Akaddas Ali contested the suit on the plea interalia, that surendra Kumar Das had purchased the land in the benami of his two sons, Subondu and Sudhendu and Surendra Kumar Das died at Shilchar before the Title Suit No. 72 of 1947 was decreed leaving behind six sons and he got the suit land by way of exchange with the sons of Surendra Das. The said suit was dismissed by the Trial Court on 31.8.61 and the defendant No. 1 professed Title Appeal No. 561/61 which was allowed on 12.4.63 by the First Court of Subordinate Judge, Sylhet and the title of the defendant No. 1 was allowed on 12.4.63 by the First Court of Subordinate Judge, Sylhet and the title of the defendant No. 1 was declared and also a decree for recovery of khas possession was granted in favour of defendant No. 1 as against the appellate decree Akaddas Ali preferred second appeal No. 968 of 1963 before the honourable High Court and the appeal was dismissed on 13.7.76. The defendant No. 1 then filed Title Execution Case No. 33 of 1977 on 27.8.77 in the Court of Sadar Munsif for execution of the decree obtained in Title Suit No. 56 of 1959 and the writ of delivery of possession was issued on 20.9.77 and the learned Advocate Commissioner and the process server of the Court went to give delivery of possession of the suit land but could not execute the writ because of the obstruction by the plaintiffs set up by the judgment debtor. The defendant No. 1 being the decree holder applied on 26.9.77 for police help and also applied on 3.11.77 under Order 21 Rule 97 C.P.C. for direction to give delivery of khas possession and the notices were served upon the plaintiffs in the said execution case and the plaintiffs appeared and filed objection on 27.12.77 claiming that they purchased the suit property from Rais Ali. The learned Munsif after hearing the parties passed any order on 21.3.1978 under Order 21 Rule 98 to the effect that the resistance or obstructions by the plaintiffs was without any just causes and directed delivery of khas possession by evicting the plaintiffs. Thereafter the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 129 of 1978 on 27.3.1978 for declaration of their title but the plaint of the suit was rejected for non-payment of deficit Court fees. The plaintiffs also preferred Civil Revision No. 425 of 1978 before the High Court Division and the Rule issued in the revision case was discharged on 25.7.78 with the finding that the plaintiffs had been set up by the judgment debtors of Title Suit No. 56/59 and they have no right, title and interest in the suit land and the judgment debtors in collusion with Assaduddin and Aftabuddin and Rais Ali have created the alleged bainapatra dated 3.4.1958 and the four registered kabalas obtained by the plaintiffs are collusive, false and fabricated. The judgment debtors with the help of the plaintiffs have been delaying and defeating the rightful claim of the defendant No. 1.
